preflight.initialReason: Issue #12 first measurement: the merge base has no local check workload. After an untimed warm-up build on both sides, time the typecheck, lint, unit and parity lanes once and measure native peak RSS. The five-minute ceiling comes from issue #12 and covers the checks with their builds; elapsed time and memory are compared with the warm merge base using a 50% margin.
preflight.changeReason: Raised from 300 s to 900 s on 2026-10-22: the checks outgrew five minutes on the reference Mac (Mac15,12, M3, 16 GB, mains power). At a036872, at load 6 to 14, the unit lane alone took about 790 s: the parallel vitest block 135 s, the one-at-a-time block 557 s (#16 339 s of it: budgets.test.ts 128 s, crash-redraft 116 s), cargo test 62 s and node --test 38 s; typecheck, lint, catalogue drift, corpus and parity add about 40 s. The files that time a frozen budget must run with nothing beside them (#664), and they alone take about 260 s, 115 s of it the fixed sleep of #16's idle-CPU test, so no schedule brings the checks under 300 s; with everything that may overlap overlapped, the floor is about 450 to 500 s. Full preflights read 706 to 1118 s, all on a loaded machine.

harness.initialReason: Issue #48 first measurement: the merge base has no harness. The lane runs only when a change touches the harness, its hook or its launch facts, since each run spends plan usage. It runs every scripted session once, on real agents, and holds each to 60 s and all of them to 10 minutes on the reference Mac. Model latency moves a single run far more than a code change does, so a later merge base's runs are compared with a 100% margin.

Measure skeleton process startup, not issue #17 hook overhead, in 20 rounds interleaved with the merge base. p50 and peak memory get a 50% relative margin and the design's 10 MB peak-memory ceiling; p95 is reported, since its tail moves past that margin between identical binaries. Established definitions are frozen.
